key_insight: A first-principles nonequilibrium BSE plus ab initio molecular dynamics framework separates electronic and thermal lattice effects in CH3NH3PbBr3 transient absorption, showing electronic screening dominates ultrafast dynamics while lattice motion takes over at longer delays.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mechanistic roadmap for interpreting pump-probe signals in perovskite solar cells and for designing materials/models that distinguish carrier-driven from thermally driven spectral changes.
method: Nonequilibrium Bethe-Salpeter equation for excited-state optical/X-ray response
Ab initio molecular dynamics to capture thermal lattice motion
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative, first-principles agreement across femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales, with distinct spectral trends assigned to electronic screening at early times and lattice effects at later times.
watch_item: The approach is computationally intensive and material-specific, so transferability to other perovskites or larger device-relevant heterostructures may require careful validation.
paper_title: Disentangling Electronic and Lattice Contributions to Transient Absorption in Metal Halide Perovskites: A First-Principles Study of CH3NH3PbBr3
